title: Four brothers at the lake
hookLine: one by one the brothers take from the yaksha's lake without asking, and why Hindus ask the earth's pardon each morning
carry: ask the earth's leave before you take

lines: THE SAME VOICE, THE SAME WORDS.
cards: Nakula doesn't come back. Under the tree, his brothers wait, and wait, and Yudhishthira sends the next one. Sahadeva, go and find your brother, and bring water.
So Sahadeva follows the cranes to the lake, and there is Nakula, lying on the bank. Sahadeva is grieving, and burning with thirst, and the voice speaks again, the same words. This lake is mine.
Answer first. Back under the tree, three brothers are still waiting for water.

teach.b: Sahadeva drinks, and falls beside his brother. Now Yudhishthira sends Arjuna, the great archer. Arjuna sees both twins dead and looks for an enemy.
When the voice speaks, he shoots at it by ear alone. The voice answers, unhurt: your arrows can't touch me. Answer my questions, and then drink.
Arjuna drinks, and falls. Then Bhima comes, the strong one, sure this is some spirit's work and ready to fight it, after a drink. The voice warns him too.
Thirst, grief, aim and strength, and not one of them asks. Listen again to what the voice said first: this lake is mine. In Hindu tradition the world is full of owners you can't see.
Rivers are goddesses. Yakshas guard lakes and trees.
The earth herself is Bhumi Devi, Mother Earth. So many Hindus begin the day with a short verse to her before their feet touch the floor, asking her to forgive them for stepping on her.
Before a house is built, a bhoomi puja asks her leave. One way to hear the lake, then: the brothers didn't fail for lack of strength.
They took without asking the owner. Four heroes of the Mahabharata lie on the shore. One brother is left.

how: In the epic, the four brothers fall one by one before Yudhishthira arrives, each warned by the same voice in the same words. Many Hindus touch the floor on waking and ask Mother Earth's pardon, and a bhoomi puja asks her leave before building.

o: a forest hermit who lives beside the water
a demon who poisons wells to trap travelers
a spirit; here, the unseen owner of the lake

games.q: the brothers at the lake — tap the pairs.
p: plans to fight, but drinks first
Mother Earth, asked for pardon each morning

s: Arjuna's arrows wounded the owner of the voice
the voice answered him, unhurt, and asked again for answers first.
Bhima meant to fight whoever had done this
but he drank before he fought, and fell.
in Hindu tradition, land and water belong to no one until we claim them
the earth is Bhumi Devi, rivers are goddesses, and a bhoomi puja asks her leave before building.

games.q: your family is breaking ground for a new house, and Nani says nobody digs until the pandit does a bhoomi puja. why?
o: it asks Bhumi Devi, Mother Earth, for leave before we take her ground, like the yaksha's lake had an owner.
it's just to bless the builders with luck.
it's a way to mark where the walls go.
games.why: the land isn't empty; it's Mother Earth. a bhoomi puja asks her leave first, the thing none of the four brothers did at the lake.

practice: Before you stand up from this, rest your fingertips on the floor, the way many Hindus do each morning. Feel the ground holding you up, as it has all day without being asked.
Breathe in, and think of one thing you'll take from the earth today: water, food, a place to walk.
If you pray, ask Bhumi Devi's pardon and thank her in your own words; if not, simply thank the ground, then touch your fingers to your heart.

wordCard.voice: Yaksha, the unseen spirit who owns the lake and asks before anyone may drink. Four brothers bring thirst, grief, aim and strength, and none of them asks the owner. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: yaksha, a powerful spirit; here the unseen owner of the lake.

carryVoice: Your line: ask the earth's leave before you take. Thirst, grief, aim and strength all came up short. Day eight hundred two, done.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Aranyaka Parva), the episode of the Yaksha's questions: Sahadeva, Arjuna and Bhima at the lake
Morning verse to Bhumi Devi asking pardon for touching her with the feet; bhoomi puja before building; rivers as goddesses; yakshas as guardians of waters and trees, in general
